title: Dependency Tree Depth Overgrowth
damaged_code:
```rust
# Map of dependencies goes 5 levels deep
direct_dep -> dep_b -> dep_c -> dep_d -> dep_e
```
pattern: Importing a large number of fine-grained packages recursively without limit, creating a highly complex dependency graph.
why_bad: It results in high maintenance overhead, extreme vulnerability to supply-chain attacks, and a massive build graph that slows down compilation.
detection: A dependency manifest where direct packages pull in a long trail of transitive packages, exceeding 3 levels of depth.
counterexample: Depending strictly on stable, consolidated standard library packages.
fix: Audit and prune the dependency tree, replacing micro-packages with direct implementations of basic tasks.
